## Overview Return HTTP 400 for nonzero effective priorities on the Python generation and pooling serving paths when priority scheduling is disabled, enforcing the existing request-field contract. ## Claims - Validate chat, completion and Responses priorities after applying existing header precedence and invalid-header fallback. - Validate body priorities on batch chat, token-input generation and shared pooling paths. - Preserve zero-priority acceptance and nonzero-priority acceptance with `--scheduling-policy priority`. ## Validation ### Tests HTTP regression, complete-module and lint validation used source matching `7b688a9e6`, based on `7050ef881`, on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. The batch-chat module uses Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; the completion module uses Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B. Unit, beam and standalone-request results were recorded against the same production code and unchanged relevant tests, using Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B where applicable. The environment used Python 3.13.16, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, official OpenAI SDK 2.54.0 and a uv-managed virtual environment. | Check | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | New unit regressions | 6 failed, 14 passed | All 20 passed within the 81-test run | | Five HTTP regressions in the batch-chat module | 5 failed with `assert 200 == 400`, 11 deselected | 5 passed, 11 deselected | | Entire changed unit files | — | 81 passed | | Entire batch-chat module, without `-k` | — | 16 passed | | Entire completion module, without `-k` | — | 25 passed | | Chat and completion beam-priority propagation | — | 6 passed | | Standalone probes with both policies | 82 HTTP 200 responses | 24 expected FCFS HTTP 400 responses; 58 HTTP 200 controls | | Accepted model-output comparison | Reference | 58/58 identical | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | — | Passed | The five HTTP cases are included in the 16-case batch-chat run. Three completion beam cases are also included in the unit-file run. The baseline used the regression tests with unchanged production source from `7050ef881`: ```bash export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py \ tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py \ -k priority_requires_priority_scheduling -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py \ -k priority_validation_http -v ``` The baseline failures reported: ```text Failed: DID NOT RAISE 6 failed, 14 passed, 61 deselected E assert 200 == 400 5 failed, 11 deselected ``` Checks with the fix: ```bash export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py \ tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py \ -k beam_search_preserves_request_priority -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py \ -k priority_validation_http -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -v .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ docs/serving/online_serving/openai_compatible_server.md \ vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py \ vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/batch_serving.py \ vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/serving.py \ vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py \ tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py ``` The HTTP regression exercises streaming chat, completions, Responses, batch chat and token-input generation through the existing batch-chat server. All five cases assert HTTP 400 and `error.param == "priority"`. Its shared fixture enables scale-out so token-input generation reaches validation. The Python chat-completion CI job selects this module; the Rust frontend job does not. The standalone probes covered chat, completions, Responses, batch chat, token-input generation, embeddings and `/pooling`. They used greedy generation and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. All 58 accepted generation or pooling outputs matched the baseline; the comparison excludes changing response-envelope fields such as IDs and timestamps. Model evaluation: not applicable. This change validates request admission without changing model computation, sampling or scheduler ordering. Real-model serving checks and accepted-output comparisons are reported above. ## Details The generation resolver returned a priority without checking the scheduler policy, while pooling and two direct generation paths forwarded body priorities unchecked. The frontend now raises `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter="priority"` before engine submission when the effective value is nonzero and the policy is not `priority`. Clients whose nonzero priorities were previously ignored under FCFS now receive the documented error. The server documentation explains the default FCFS behavior and how to enable priority scheduling. Header precedence and invalid-header fallback remain unchanged on chat, completions and Responses. Batch chat, token-input generation and pooling retain body-only priority handling. This change covers the Python serving paths described above. Renderer-only endpoints, offline APIs, the Rust frontend, generative scoring and structured decisions are outside its scope. Saved open-PR searches for `priority fcfs`, `priority validation scheduling`, `"non-zero" "priority" "scheduling"`, `"priority" "reject" "fcfs"` and `"X-Vllm-Priority"` found no matching policy-validation fix. [#62727](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62727) addresses batch-header propagation, and [#62253](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62253) addressed beam-priority propagation. This change does not duplicate either propagation fix. AI assistance was used to develop and review this change. ---
